newsitem.title: USA: Kmart sales gains boost second-quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Kmart sales gains boost second-quarter profit.

text.p: Kmart Corp., the nation's third-largest retailer, said Thursday that strong sales of most merchandise pushed second-quarter profits up 35 percent, slightly exceeding Wall Street estimates.
Kmart's income from continuing operations rose to $31 million, or 6 cents a share, in the quarter ended July 30, from $23 million, or 5 cents a share, a year earlier.

The results excluded Kmart's Builders Square home improvement chain, which was sold in July to investment bank Leonard Green & Partners. With Builders Square included, the year-ago net income was $34 million, or 7 cents a share.

The profit topped average forecasts of 4 cents a share published by First Call, which tracks profit estimates. The estimates, however, had been revised downward last month when Kmart said it expected to turn in results below last year's.
Kmart stock rose $1.125 to $12.875 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the fourth most active issue with almost 5.8 million shares changing hands.

Analysts said Kmart's earnings would have been far higher had it not been for problems in its women's clothing business where its fashion-oriented offerings turned off customers. Markdowns to clear slow-selling items slashed gross profit margin to 21 percent from 22.3 percent a year earlier.
Kmart's apparel chief resigned in June and was replaced Monday with former Hills Stores Co. President E. Jackson Smailes.
Kmart executives told analysts they believe the markdowns are mostly over and that they expect women's apparel sales to be flat during the third quarter and to improve in the fourth quarter.

"They are optimistic that the women's business won't be the disaster in the second half of the year that it was in the first half," said Prudential Securities analyst L. Wayne Hood. "They have to improve sales and margins in women's apparel business."
Kmart continued to make progress cutting costs, reducing selling, general and administrative expenses by $42 million to $1.5 billion in the quarter.
Sales rose 3.7 percent to $7.85 billion from $7.57 billion. Sales at stores open at least a year rose 5.6 percent.

"Most Kmart merchandise categories reported improved sales performance thus far this year, led by housewares, and home decor, cosmetics and fragrances, and consumables," Kmart Chairman Floyd Hall said in a statement.
Kmart is working to convert its stores to a new format, called Big Kmart, which will emphasize quick-selling items such as soft drinks, snacks and household cleaning products.
With 2,122 Kmart, Big Kmart and Super Kmart outlets, the company is third-largest U.S. retailer after Wal-Mart Stores Inc. and Sears, Roebuck & Co.
